rubrics.criterion: All six command gateways that absorbed lower-layer machinery — the string write generic, the string read generic, and the numeric generic behind the string family, the expiry mutation generic and the TTL query generic in the database module, and the hash field increment handler in the hash module (the functions named in the responsibility manifest) — no longer hold an inlined re-implementation of the shared pipeline stages inside the handler body; each now reads as orchestration over dedicated units, and no handler left in those files still carries a multi-layer monolith body.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's central obligation: the injected campaign expanded exactly these six shared handlers into deep-inline monoliths, so the task is complete only when every one of the six — not one convenient example — has its layering restored, whichever named units the solver uses to do it.

rubrics.criterion: Each duplicated pipeline stage resolves to one shared implementation used by the affected families — the same stage (for example the lazy-expiry check, the key lookup, the add/overwrite assignment, or integer reply construction) is not left as two or more per-command private variants carrying the same logic.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt asks for one shared implementation per stage; a repair that fragments the machine into per-command copies would keep the maintenance trap the request is about even though the monolith functions are gone.

rubrics.criterion: The re-layered handlers preserve the direction-specific semantics of the paths through the re-extracted units: read-side commands keep their miss replies (bulk null for GET-style reads and the -1/-2 sentinel replies for the TTL query) and read-path hit/miss statistics, while write-side commands keep write-path lookup behavior with the reference-cache refresh and the modified-key notification; the expiry mutation generic still rewrites the command to a DEL and propagates it to the append-only file and replicas exactly once per executed operation.
rubrics.rationale: These coupled obligations ride on the exact delegation choices the repair must make per family; restoring the boundaries without reconnecting the direction-specific versions of the pipeline stages is the most likely incomplete repair for this instance because ordinary calls in all directions still succeed.

rubrics.criterion: Any new units introduced by the repair are placed coherently within the existing module structure and are adopted by every affected family that needs the same stage, and the repair does not bypass existing shared routines by introducing a near-duplicate unit alongside them.
rubrics.rationale: The change must remain one coherent re-layering of the command layer; introducing parallel near-duplicates of capabilities the server already owns would recreate the disease in a different shape while appearing to complete the task.

rubrics.criterion: The campaign's scaffolding is gone from the touched files: the extra forward declarations for reply and cluster bookkeeping helpers that only the unfolded bodies needed, and the parsing include added to the two modules that previously had no such usage, are removed or demonstrably still used — no header residue survives that exists solely to support the removed inline code.
rubrics.rationale: The injection left distinct residue in all three touched modules; a complete refactor of this instance returns those header regions to their campaign-free state rather than only editing function bodies.

rubrics.criterion: The patch contains a rename-only or move-only pseudo-fix: at least one of the six monolith bodies survives nearly unchanged under a different unit name (for example an identical body hoisted into a same-module helper with a suffix-style name, wrapped by the original gateway name), so the absorbed multi-layer machinery still exists as one oversized body instead of being re-shared through the layers.
rubrics.rationale: This is the most plausible cosmetic completion for this instance: pushing a body into an adjacent function satisfies the 'gateway functions should look thin' reading while keeping the deep-inline duplication intact, and a text-level rename is exactly what the injected step-marker comments invite.

rubrics.criterion: The observable accounting still happens exactly as before the patch at the same logical events: key hit/miss statistics, the expired-keys counter, the dirty counter, the reference-cache clock refresh, modified-key notifications for WATCH semantics, and append-only-file/replica propagation of synthesized delete commands neither double-fire nor go missing on any executed command path.
rubrics.rationale: The re-extraction moves the points where side effects live; the duplicated fragments made several accounting steps manual, so a repair that re-wires the stages can silently drop or duplicate them, and the test suite's aggregate coverage does not pin every one of these observably.

rubrics.criterion: Reply and error behavior remains byte-identical on the special-state edges of these families: expired keys behave as missing for conditional operations, missing versus present-without-expiry keys yield their sentinel replies, wrong-type accesses and parse failures yield the original messages, numeric overflow keeps its error and bounds behavior, and reply formatting (bulk headers, integer framing, error prefixes) still takes the same forms.
rubrics.rationale: The inlined copies embed the reply machinery's internals per site; re-sharing them is where formatting drift most plausibly enters, and case-specific edge replies (the TTL sentinels, the overflow errors, the conditional-create rejection) are the exact observables that must not drift.

rubrics.criterion: The patch introduces a silent behavior drift that ordinary calls would not expose: for example an expired key treated as existing by the conditional paths, expiry propagation running before the key is determined deleted, a reference leak or double free around the objects handed to the re-shared units, or the hash field-write path no longer converting from its compact encoding when the size threshold is crossed.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible-looking re-layering can pass ordinary command flows while breaking on special state (expired keys, object ownership across unit boundaries, hash encoding conversion); naming this instance's concrete drift paths keeps the grader from accepting a subtly broken repair.
